evidence.quote: In practice, how much each modality is trusted at a given location is decided by learned weights that are neither characterized nor auditable.
We label every ground-truth object by which modalities detected it, then mine the resulting 0.4M-object database across nuScenes, KITTI, and Waymo.

solution.summary: The modality-preference boundary tracks the object itself: a traffic cone is nearly six times as likely as a truck to be seen by the camera alone (16.8% vs. 2.9%), regardless of range.
solution.approach: The modality-preference boundary tracks the object itself: a traffic cone is nearly six times as likely as a truck to be seen by the camera alone (16.8% vs. 2.9%), regardless of range.
components: Camera-only detections peak at 10-30 m, inside the band usually ceded to LiDAR, and fall away on either side.
The drivers of failure are not additive either: the distance×density interaction alone outweighs the entire main effect of viewing direction.
We further find that modality dominance is directionally nonstationary, with objects behind the vehicle being markedly more LiDAR-dominant than those in front.
